parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/order/order.service.ts is in the application layer (it matches *.service.ts). Its job is to coordinate order use cases. create() checks the input, builds the entity through the injected repository and saves it. findOne() loads an order and turns a missing record into a not-found error. Calling an injected repository is normal coordination work for an application service. The file builds no raw queries, sets up no connections and does no mapping, so it carries no infrastructure logic. It has no routing, request parsing or response shaping, so it carries no presentation logic. Two parts are borderline. First, BadRequestException and NotFoundException come from Nest's HTTP layer, so they lean toward transport. In NestJS services this is the standard pattern, and these are thrown errors rather than transport handling. Second, the quantity check and the total calculation (quantity * unitPrice) could live on the domain entity. They are small, though, and a use case can reasonably hold them. Neither is clearly a responsibility that belongs to another layer kind. No ADR text was provided to say otherwise.
